t: You're at the Greenwich Foot Tunnel, which crosses beneath the River Thames in East London. It was designed by Sir Alexander Richardson Binnie, a British civil engineer who lived from 1839 to 1917. Binnie was responsible for several major engineering projects, including a number connected with crossings of the Thames in London, and this tunnel is one of them. So when you walk through, you're using the work of an engineer who spent his career helping people get across the river.
